standard_prerequisites: derived pushforward Rf_* along a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces
vanishing and quasi-coherence of higher direct images from the cohomology of spaces chapter, stable under base change
the two-spectral-sequence for the derived functor of a complex of functors
K-injective resolution application giving R Gamma(V, Rf_*E) = R Gamma(V x_Y X, E)
truncation triangles in the derived category
core_obligations: Prove: (1) Rf_* sends D_QCoh(O_X) into D_QCoh(O_Y); (2) for Y quasi-compact there is N with H^m(Rf_*E)=0 for m >= N whenever E in D_QCoh has H^m(E)=0 for m>0; (3) N can be chosen uniformly over all base changes Y' to Y
proof_roadmap: Locality on Y reduces to Y quasi-compact; pick N from the vanishing lemma for higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules, valid under base change, with R^p f_*F quasi-coherent for all p
Bounded below case: the spectral sequence R^p f_* H^q(E) implies R^{p+q} f_*E with quasi-coherent entries vanishing for p >= N yields (1) and the bounds in (2) and (3)

For (2) and (3) with E concentrated in degrees <= 0: for V affine in Y_etale the K-injective application lemma identifies R Gamma(V, Rf_*E) with R Gamma(V x_Y X, E), whose cohomology vanishes in degrees >= N by the application lemma; this for all V gives the vanishing of H^m(Rf_*E) for m >= N

General (1): truncate E; by (2) the cohomology of Rf_* of the low truncation vanishes in high degrees, so each R^q f_*E agrees with R^q f_* of a bounded truncation, where quasi-coherence was already shown
difficulty_reason: H2: a standard three-part argument combining a spectral sequence, K-injective section comparison and truncation; every step is written out with its quoted lemma.
